content: This guideline, titled Protecting, Promoting, and Supporting Breastfeeding in Facilities Providing Maternity and Newborn Services, was published by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2017. It serves as an update to the Ten Steps to Successful Breastfeeding, originally published in 1989 as a joint statement by WHO and UNICEF. This updated guideline complements the operational guidance of the Innocenti Declaration on the Protection, Promotion, and Support of Breastfeeding (1990) and the Innocenti Declaration 2005 on Infant and Young Child Feeding. It also aligns with the Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative (BFHI), first introduced in 1991 and updated in 2009, where relevant aspects of the Ten Steps remain unchanged. The document was developed following rigorous procedures outlined in the WHO Handbook for Guideline Development. It incorporates direct and indirect evidence, as well as qualitative reviews, to inform its recommendations. The guideline expands on dissemination strategies and addresses ethical and equity considerations, as summarized in recent reviews on these topics. The preparation of this guideline was coordinated by the WHO Evidence and Programme Guidance Unit, Department of Nutrition for Health and Development, under the leadership of Dr. Pura Rayco-Solon and Dr. Juan Pablo Peña-Rosas. WHO acknowledges the technical guidance provided by members of the WHO steering committee for this normative work, including experts from various departments and organizations such as UNICEF. The guideline development process involved contributions from numerous individuals and organizations. Technical input was provided by members of the WHO guideline development group, systematic review teams, and external resource persons. Peer reviewers and members of the WHO Guidelines Review Committee also offered valuable feedback. The guideline development group meetings were chaired by experts in the field, and systematic reviews were conducted to ensure evidence-based recommendations. Financial support for this work was provided by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, Nutrition International, and the International Micronutrient Malnutrition Prevention and Control Programme of the United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). These donors did not influence the guideline development process, including the formulation of research questions, systematic reviews, or recommendations. The guideline emphasizes the importance of breastfeeding as a cornerstone of child survival, nutrition, development, and maternal health. It aligns with the global nutrition targets for 2025, which include increasing the rate of exclusive breastfeeding in the first six months to at least 50%. To support women and optimize breastfeeding practices, WHO and UNICEF published the original joint statement in 1989, which outlined the Ten Steps to Successful Breastfeeding. This updated guideline builds on that foundation, providing evidence-based recommendations to protect, promote, and support breastfeeding in maternity and newborn care facilities.
